body:
This PR adds comprehensive breaking change documentation for the removal of `project.json` support from `dotnet restore` in .NET 10 Preview 7.

## Changes Made

**New Breaking Change Document**: Created complete documentation following the standard Microsoft breaking change format at `/docs/core/compatibility/sdk/10.0/dotnet-restore-project-json-unsupported.md` including:
- Clear description of the breaking change behavior
- Proper categorization as a "Source incompatible" change  
- Historical context about project.json deprecation since 2017
- Migration guidance pointing to legacy `dotnet migrate` command and PackageReference format
- Reference to official NuGet migration documentation

**Updated Documentation Index**: Added the new breaking change to the main compatibility table in `/docs/core/compatibility/10.0.md` under the SDK and MSBuild section with proper ordering and categorization.

**Updated Table of Contents**: Added the new entry to `/docs/core/compatibility/toc.yml` in the appropriate alphabetical position within the SDK and MSBuild section for .NET 10.

## Validation

- ✅ Follows Microsoft documentation style guidelines from `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- ✅ Uses the breaking change template from `.github/prompts/breaking-change.md`
- ✅ Markdown syntax validated with markdownlint-cli2
- ✅ All internal links verified to exist
- ✅ Consistent formatting with existing breaking change documentation

The documentation properly explains that starting with .NET 10 Preview 7, `dotnet restore` will ignore `project.json` based projects rather than restoring their dependencies, completing the transition away from the format that was deprecated in 2017 and replaced by PackageReference.

Fixes #47968.

author: ootakazuhiko
body:
## Summary
- Add comprehensive Claude Code Task Tool integration for Phase 2 (Natural Language Requirements) processing
- Implement NaturalLanguageTaskAdapter with advanced requirements analysis capabilities
- Enhance CLI with natural language processing commands

## Key Features

### Natural Language Processing Capabilities
- **Requirements Analysis**: Comprehensive processing of natural language requirements with gap identification
- **Entity Extraction**: Automatic extraction of business entities and relationships from requirements text
- **Completeness Validation**: Coverage analysis for functional, non-functional, business, and technical requirements
- **Ambiguity Resolution**: Detection and resolution of ambiguous requirement statements
- **Requirements Structuring**: Organization and categorization of requirements by type and priority

### Claude Code Task Tool Integration
- Full integration with Claude Code's Task tool for seamless developer workflows
- Proactive guidance system that intervenes when requirements are incomplete or ambiguous
- Automatic task classification and routing based on user intent
- Comprehensive response format with analysis, recommendations, and next actions

### CLI Enhancement
New `ae-framework natural-language` command with options:
- `--analyze`: Analyze natural language requirements for completeness and consistency
- `--extract-entities`: Extract business entities and relationships from requirements
- `--validate-completeness`: Validate requirements coverage across all categories
- `--sources <sources>`: Specify source files or text to process

### Example Usage
```bash
# Analyze requirements from markdown file
ae-framework natural-language --analyze --sources="requirements.md"

# Extract business entities from specifications
ae-framework natural-language --extract-entities --sources="specs.txt"

# Validate completeness of requirements coverage
ae-framework natural-language --validate-completeness
```

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **NaturalLanguageTaskAdapter**: Core adapter class implementing Task Tool interface
- **TaskRequest/TaskResponse**: Standardized interfaces for Claude Code integration
- **RequirementDocument**: Structured representation of processed requirements
- **ProcessedRequirements**: Comprehensive analysis results with gaps and conflicts

### Task Classification System
Intelligent task routing based on description and prompt analysis:
- `analyze-requirements`: Full requirements analysis workflow
- `extract-entities`: Business entity identification and modeling
- `validate-completeness`: Coverage and completeness validation
- `resolve-ambiguity`: Ambiguity detection and resolution
- `structure-requirements`: Requirements organization and categorization
- `identify-gaps`: Gap analysis and missing requirement identification

### Proactive Guidance
- Real-time monitoring of development activity
- Automatic intervention for incomplete requirements
- Suggestions for requirement clarification and improvement
- Prevention of progress blocking when critical issues are detected

## Test Plan
- [x] Task adapter initialization and configuration
- [x] CLI command integration and argument parsing
- [x] Task classification and routing logic
- [x] Response formatting and display
- [x] Error handling and graceful degradation
- [ ] Integration testing with existing ae-framework phases
- [ ] End-to-end workflow testing with sample requirements

## Integration Points
- Seamless integration with existing Phase 1 (Intent) workflows
- Preparation for Phase 3 (User Stories) handoff
- Support for Phase 4 (Validation) traceability requirements
- Foundation for Phase 5 (Domain Modeling) entity extraction

author: taylordotfish
body:
Add a new reference-counted shared pointer type, `bun.ptr.Shared`.

Features:

* Can hold data of any type; doesn't require adding a `ref_count` field
* Reference count is an internal implementation detail; will never get out of sync due to erroneous manipulation
* Supports weak pointers
* Supports optional pointers with no overhead (`Shared(?*T)` is the same size as `Shared(*T)`)
* Has an atomic thread-safe version: `bun.ptr.AtomicShared`
* Defaults to `bun.default_allocator`, but can handle other allocators as well, with both static and dynamic polymorphism

The following types are now deprecated and will eventually be removed:

* `bun.ptr.RefCount`
* `bun.ptr.ThreadSafeRefCount`
* `bun.ptr.RefPtr`
* `bun.ptr.WeakPtr`

(For internal tracking: fixes STAB-1011)

author: copilot
body:
When belts are fully retracted, the Maslow CNC system repeatedly logs the error message:

```
[MSG:ERR: MaslowKinematics: Failed to compute X,Y from belt lengths, using (0,0)]
```

This error spam occurs because the kinematic solver cannot determine a valid X,Y position when belts are retracted, which is expected and normal behavior. The error message provides no useful information in this context and clutters the console output.

## Solution

Modified `MaslowKinematics::transform_motors_to_cartesian()` to check the current calibration state before logging kinematic computation failures. The error message is now suppressed when the system is in `RETRACTING` or `RETRACTED` states, where kinematic failures are expected.

## Technical Details

- Added state check using `Maslow.calibration.getCurrentState()`
- Preserves error logging for legitimate kinematic failures in all other states
- Minimal performance impact (state check only occurs when computation already failed)
- Uses existing calibration state machine without introducing new dependencies

## Code Changes

```cpp
// Don't spam the console during belt retraction - this is expected behavior
int currentState = Maslow.calibration.getCurrentState();
if (currentState != RETRACTING && currentState != RETRACTED) {
    log_error("MaslowKinematics: Failed to compute X,Y from belt lengths, using (0,0)");
}
```

The change is surgical and maintains all existing functionality while eliminating unnecessary console noise during normal belt retraction operations.

Fixes #257.

author: yichuan-w
body:
# Fix hidden-path indexing with opt-in `--include-hidden` flag

## Summary
- **Default behavior:** Hidden files/dirs (e.g., `.github`) remain excluded.  
- **New flag:** `--include-hidden` (`BooleanOptionalAction`, default `false`) allows including hidden paths.  
- **Implementation details:**  
  - Pass `exclude_hidden = not include_hidden` to `SimpleDirectoryReader` for directory scans and PDF fallback.  
  - Hidden files explicitly listed via `--docs` are still honored, but filtered out if `--include-hidden` is not set.  

## Rationale
Previously, running:  
```bash
leann build test-indexing-yml --docs ./.github/workflows
```  
would load **0 docs**, because LlamaIndex excludes hidden paths by default.  

## Usage Examples
- **Default (exclude hidden):**  
  ```bash
  leann build my-index --docs .github/workflows
  ```  
- **Include hidden:**  
  ```bash
  leann build my-index --docs .github/workflows --include-hidden
  ```  

## Testing
- Verified locally:  
  - Default: `.github/workflows` → 0 docs loaded.  
  - With `--include-hidden`: 4 `.yml` docs discovered, indexed, and chunked.  

## Notes
- Closes **#52**.  
- No breaking changes — default behavior unchanged.

body:
## Summary
- Add comprehensive Claude Code Task Tool integration for Phase 3 (User Stories Creation) processing
- Implement UserStoriesTaskAdapter with advanced user story management capabilities
- Enable seamless story generation, validation, prioritization, and estimation workflows

## Key Features

### User Story Management Capabilities
- **Story Generation**: Automatic generation of well-structured user stories from requirements
- **Story Validation**: INVEST criteria compliance checking and quality assessment
- **Story Prioritization**: Business value-based prioritization with release planning
- **Story Estimation**: Complexity analysis and effort distribution with story points
- **Acceptance Criteria Creation**: Given-When-Then format with comprehensive test scenarios
- **Epic Organization**: Logical grouping of stories with bounded context alignment
- **Dependency Analysis**: Critical path analysis and cross-story relationship management

### Claude Code Task Tool Integration
- Full integration with Claude Code's Task tool for seamless agile workflows
- Proactive guidance system for story quality and completeness issues
- Intelligent task classification based on user intent and context
- Comprehensive analysis reports with recommendations and actionable next steps

### Advanced Story Processing
**Story Generation**:
- Transform natural language requirements into structured user stories
- Automatic epic creation and story organization
- Priority assignment based on business value analysis
- Story point estimation with complexity breakdown

**Story Validation**:
- INVEST criteria compliance checking (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable)
- Format validation for proper user story structure
- Acceptance criteria completeness validation
- Cross-story dependency validation

**Story Prioritization**:
- Business value matrix analysis
- Release planning with delivery timeline estimation
- Risk factor identification and mitigation strategies
- Stakeholder value alignment assessment

**Story Estimation**:
- Story point assignment with complexity analysis
- Effort distribution across team capacity
- Velocity-based planning and forecasting
- Confidence levels for estimation accuracy

### CLI Enhancement
Enhanced `ae-framework user-stories` command with comprehensive options:
- `--generate`: Generate user stories from requirements with epic organization
- `--validate`: Validate existing user stories against INVEST criteria
- `--prioritize`: Prioritize stories using business value matrix
- `--estimate`: Estimate story complexity with points assignment
- `--sources <sources>`: Specify source files or requirements to process

### Example Usage
```bash
# Generate user stories from requirements
ae-framework user-stories --generate --sources="requirements.md"

# Validate existing user stories for quality
ae-framework user-stories --validate --sources="backlog.json"

# Prioritize stories for release planning
ae-framework user-stories --prioritize --sources="stories.md"

# Estimate story complexity and effort
ae-framework user-stories --estimate --sources="user-stories.txt"
```

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **UserStoriesTaskAdapter**: Core adapter implementing Task Tool interface
- **UserStory Interface**: Comprehensive story structure with all INVEST criteria
- **UserStorySet**: Collection with metrics, completeness scoring, and gap analysis
- **AcceptanceCriteria**: Given-When-Then format with test scenario generation

### Task Classification System
Intelligent routing for user story operations:
- `generate-stories`: Full story generation from requirements
- `validate-stories`: INVEST criteria and quality validation
- `prioritize-stories`: Business value prioritization and release planning
- `estimate-stories`: Complexity estimation and story pointing
- `create-acceptance-criteria`: Detailed criteria creation with test scenarios
- `organize-epics`: Epic creation and story organization
- `identify-dependencies`: Dependency analysis and critical path identification

### Quality Metrics
- **Format Compliance**: Proper "As a... I want... So that..." structure
- **Acceptance Criteria Coverage**: Completeness of acceptance conditions
- **Testability Score**: Measurability and verification capability
- **Independence Rating**: Story autonomy and minimal dependencies
- **Estimability Index**: Clarity for effort estimation

### Proactive Guidance
- Quality assessment with automatic intervention for poor stories
- Completeness monitoring with gap identification
- Dependency conflict detection and resolution
- Epic organization suggestions for better structure

## Integration Points
- Seamless handoff from Phase 2 (Natural Language Requirements)
- Preparation for Phase 4 (Validation) with traceability support
- Foundation for Phase 5 (Domain Modeling) with entity extraction
- Integration with existing TDD workflows for test-driven development

## Test Plan
- [x] User story generation from sample requirements
- [x] INVEST criteria validation logic
- [x] Priority matrix and business value calculations
- [x] Story point estimation algorithms
- [x] Acceptance criteria generation
- [x] Epic organization and dependency analysis
- [ ] Integration testing with Phase 2 requirements
- [ ] End-to-end workflow testing with sample backlog

The changes include:

  - Stop invoking the closed loop algorithm from the UI

Stopping closed loop invocation from the UI is to avoid changing the PID controller's state until there is a heartbeat (either CGM or pump)

author: apialanag
body:
This commit fixes the payment redirection issue caused by the browser's user gesture security policy.

The previous implementation failed because the delay between the user's click and the redirection was too long. The new implementation opens a new window immediately upon the user's click and then redirects that new window once the payment URL is fetched. This ensures the redirection is not blocked by popup blockers.

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature
/kind api-change

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR implements the new unified list query, pagination, sorting, and filtering system for the Service Grid suite (Services), completing the service networking functionality following the same architectural pattern established in foundation/PR1/PR2/PR3/PR4/PR5.

**Backend Changes:**
- Add unified `ListQuery` parameter parsing for Service handlers
- Implement `ListResponse` with pagination metadata (total, page, pageSize, hasNext)
- Create resource-specific transform logic in `transform.go`:
  - `ServiceListItem` DTO with projection, field getters, and comparators
  - Enhanced Service display with Type, ClusterIP, ExternalIP, Ports, and Age fields
  - Smart handling of LoadBalancer ingress and external IP configurations
- Support server-side filtering, sorting, and pagination using `common` functions
- Maintain full compatibility with existing Kubernetes Service resources

**Frontend Changes:**
- Replace old TableCard pagination with new unified pagination controls
- Add state management for page, pageSize, sort, order, and filter parameters
- Implement new MUI-based pagination UI with dropdowns and navigation
- Update API hooks to accept query parameters object instead of single namespace
- Update column definitions to handle both original and transformed data types
- Add comprehensive Service information display including networking details:
  - Service Type (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName)
  - Cluster IP and External IP addresses
  - Port configurations with protocol information
  - Service Age calculation
- Update TypeScript types to match new ListResponse format

**Key Features:**
- Consistent pagination UI across Service resources
- Server-side filtering with wildcard support (`name:*pattern*`)
- Configurable page sizes (5, 10, 20, 50)
- Sortable by name, type, clusterIP, and creationTimestamp
- Ascending/descending order support
- Enhanced Service networking information display
- Smart port formatting (name:port/protocol)
- External IP detection for LoadBalancer and ExternalIP services
- Real-time age calculation for services
- Optimized frontend-backend communication with DTOs
- Direct Kubernetes Service integration without mock dependencies

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

This PR completes the service grid suite (Services) following the established architectural pattern from foundation/PR1/PR2/PR3/PR4/PR5. All six PRs (node-suite, application-suite, config-suite, device-suite, edge-cloud-message-suite, service-grid-suite) can be merged without conflicts as verified by merge simulation in the `test-merge-simulation` branch.

The implementation includes:
1. **Enhanced Service display**: Unlike basic resource lists, Services require special handling for networking information including ports, IPs, and load balancer configurations
2. **Smart data transformation**: Complex Kubernetes Service port arrays are intelligently formatted for user-friendly display
3. **Network-aware filtering**: Supports filtering by service type, cluster IP, and external IP configurations
4. **Real data integration**: Works directly with live Kubernetes Service resources without requiring mock data
5. **Performance optimization**: Server-side pagination reduces data transfer for clusters with many services

The service grid functionality enables users to manage Kubernetes networking services with comprehensive information display and the same modern pagination, sorting, and filtering capabilities available for other resource types. This is particularly valuable for understanding service networking topology in Kubernetes/KubeEdge environments.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Services page now features improved pagination, sorting, and filtering controls with enhanced networking information display. Users can now:
- Configure page size (5/10/20/50 items per page)
- Sort by name, service type, cluster IP, or creation timestamp in ascending/descending order
- Filter services by name with wildcard support
- Navigate through pages with improved pagination controls
- View comprehensive service networking information including Type, Cluster IP, External IP, Ports, and Age
- See smart port formatting with protocol information (e.g., "http:80/TCP", "https:443/TCP")
- Identify external access points for LoadBalancer and ExternalName services
- Experience faster loading with optimized data transfer
- Access real Kubernetes Service data with consistent UI across all resource types
```

body:
This PR addresses the scattered type conversion logic across multiple files by creating a centralized, extensible type conversion system.

## Problem

Type conversion logic for converting between Python, C, and internal C# types was scattered across multiple files with duplicated hardcoded logic:

- **DotWrap.MSBuild/MethodBuilderContext.cs**: Hardcoded Python-to-C parameter conversion with repeated `if/else` blocks
- **DotWrap.Shared/PythonInteropUtils.cs**: Hardcoded C-to-Python return value conversion with pattern matching
- **DotWrap.Generator/MethodBuilderContext.cs**: Hardcoded exposed-to-internal C# type conversion
- **DotWrap.MSBuild/DotWrapObjectExtensions.cs**: Various type mapping methods

This made adding new types difficult and led to inconsistent handling across different conversion scenarios.

## Solution

Created a centralized type conversion system with:

### Core Architecture
- **`ITypeConverter`** interface for implementing type-specific conversion logic
- **`TypeConversionService`** as the main coordinator for all conversions
- **`ConversionContext`** to specify conversion direction (Python→C, C→Python, Exposed→Internal)
- **Individual type converters** for each supported type

### Type Converters Implemented
- **StringTypeConverter**: Handles string ↔ char* conversions
- **BooleanTypeConverter**: Handles bool ↔ int conversions  
- **CharacterTypeConverter**: Handles char ↔ ord/chr conversions
- **EnumTypeConverter**: Handles enum value conversions
- **HalfTypeConverter**: Handles System.Half special cases
- **ComplexObjectTypeConverter**: Handles wrapped object pointer management

### Key Features
- **Context-aware conversions**: Different logic for parameters vs return values vs nullable types
- **Consistent nullable handling**: Unified null checks across all conversion scenarios
- **Extensible design**: Easy to add new types by implementing `ITypeConverter`
- **Backward compatible**: All existing public APIs remain unchanged

## Example

Before (scattered across multiple files):
```csharp
// In MethodBuilderContext.cs
if (definition.FullyQualifiedName.Equals("string", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
{
    typedVarAssignment = $"{param.Name}{Typed} = {Ffi}.new(\"char[]\", {param.Name}.encode(\"utf-8\"))";
}
else if (definition.FullyQualifiedName.Equals("bool", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
{
    typedVarAssignment = $"{param.Name}{Typed} = int({param.Name})";
}
// ... more hardcoded logic

// In PythonInteropUtils.cs  
var resultAssignment = typeDefinition switch
{
    _ when typeDefinition.FullyQualifiedName.Equals("string", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) 
        => $"{ExportedPyResult} = str(CString({InternalPyResult}))",
    _ when typeDefinition.FullyQualifiedName.Equals("bool", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) 
        => $"{ExportedPyResult} = bool({InternalPyResult})",
    // ... more duplicated logic
};
```

After (centralized):
```csharp
// Single call handles all conversion scenarios
var conversion = ConversionService.ConvertParameterPythonToC(
    param.Name, definition, param.Type.IsNullable, isOutParameter);
```

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests for the type conversion system covering:
- String, boolean, character, enum, and complex object conversions
- Nullable type handling with proper null checks
- Different conversion directions (Python↔C, C↔Python)

Fixes #2.

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/23470

**What I did**
Keep track of how many VNET mappings are using a given PA validation entry. When deleting the last VNET mapping using a given PA validation entry, also delete the entry.

For this to work, the delete op for a VNET mapping must have the `underlay_ip` protobuf field filled.

Also add CRM checks to the DashVnetOrch unit tests.

**Why I did it**
Fix inaccurate CRM use stats.

**How I verified it**
Run the unit tests.

author: andrew-s-rosen
body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for setting the center-of-mass momentum to zero or angular momenta to zero following the creation of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution. Without these features, you can get drift of the center-of-mass like shown below or rotation of the structure. The default behavior of the `MDCalc` remains unchanged.

![test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f36bd07-6393-4ba8-82b9-2ae103d05f7e)

Additional discussion:

- https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/issues/1727
- https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/merge_requests/3793

- [X] Type annotations included. Check with `mypy`.

author: michaelorlov
body:
## Description

Add recorder event notifier class, which will be responsible for sending events on predefined topics about bag split and statistics about messages lost on transport and inner recorder level.

This PR is needed as part of the #2007 
>  2. Incremental statistics about the number of messages lost and bytes written on a per-topic basis should be published on a specific topic when messages are lost.

The `RecorderEventNotifier` class implemented as an extended replacement of the Messages Lost Notifier described in the 
[statistics_about_lost_and_recorded_messages.md](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/7f304136062740cc718502dc4a855f79aa0571a3/docs/design/statistics_about_lost_and_recorded_messages.md?plain=1#L76C1-L108) design document.
```markdown
### 4. Messages Lost Notifier

   Will need to add a new `MessagesLostNotifier` class to the `rosbag2_transport::recorder` that 
   will publish on a predefined topic, incremental statistics about the number of lost messages 
   and bytes written on a per-topic basis when messages lost happened.
   - To facilitate this, the Rosbag2 recorder shall satisfy the following requirements:
      1. The messages lost event shall be published from the Rosbag2 recorder on a dedicated topic.
      e.g., `/events/rosbag2_messages_lost`
      2. The messages lost event shall include per-topic statistics with the number of lost 
        messages. The message type could be named as `rosbag2_interfaces::msg::MessagesLostEvent`
        and defined in the `rosbag2_interfaces` package. The message type will be similar to the 
        `rosbag2_interfaces::msg::WriteSplitEvent` message type and shall contain the following 
         fields:
         - `node_name` (string): The name of the node that is recording.
         - Array of the following fields:
         - `topic_name` (string): The name of the topic on which the messages were lost.
         - `messages_lost_in_transport` (uint64_t): The number of messages lost since the last 
           event on a DDS transport layer.
         - `messages_lost_in_recorder` (uint64_t): The number of messages lost since the last 
           event in the Rosbag2 recorder.
```

Besides the functionality for the message lost notification on a dedicated topic, the `RecorderEventNotifier` also encapsulates functionality for other event notifications, such as notifications about bag split. 
Notice that notifications about bag splits were built into the `RecorderImpl` class itself. Now that functionality was moved with minimum changes to the `RecorderEventNotifier` class. A queue was added for the bag_split events to avoid missing notifications when events happened one-to-one, with minimum delay.

**Note: In this PR, the `RecorderEventNotifier` doesn't implement the core functionality of the `Messages Lost Notifier` described in the [statistics_about_lost_and_recorded_messages.md](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/rolling/docs/design/statistics_about_lost_and_recorded_messages.md) design document. However, it is a one-to-one replacement of the current implementation for the logic of what we have in the `RecorderImpl` class. That was made on purpose to be able to backport this PR to Kilted and Jazzy with minimum changes to reduce divergencies in the code base.
We will be able to backport the part related to the moving bag split event notification and callbacks for messages lost in the transport layer. However, the part related to the callbacks from the writer about lost messages will be omitted since the underlying API in the writer is missing.
The rest of the missing functionality for the `Messages Lost Notifier` will be implemented in follow-up PRs.**


<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.*
-->

Fixes # (issue) N/A
- Relates  #2007

### Is this user-facing behavior change?
No.

### Did you use Generative AI?
Yes, I am using GitHub Copilot, GPT-4.1 in my workflow.

### Additional Information
- Can be backported. Please refer to the notes above.
- It was considered to make one universal `EventNotifier` class for Player and Recorder. However, this design option was not accepted because events are very specific to the Player and Recorder classes, and it will be a cleaner implementation if they are split into separate classes. Having a common `EventNotifierBase` class also will not give much benefits, but rather will introduce extra layers of dependencies, which is unnecessary in this particular case.

author: vaibhav541
body:
## Problem
The application is experiencing high CPU usage leading to pod restarts. This is caused by an unoptimized graph processing algorithm that creates excessive CPU load through multiple uncontrolled threads.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms rate limiting between processing iterations
- Implemented 5-second timeout for long-running calculations
- Reduced path finding max_depth from 10 to 5

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core functionality remains intact
- Tested pod stability under load

## Impact
This change will significantly reduce CPU usage and prevent pod restarts while maintaining essential functionality. The trade-off is slightly reduced graph processing capacity, which is acceptable given the stability improvements.

author: mcbridejc
body:
Add definition of bootloader objects, and support for domains. This led to a large refactor of the object implementation. 

Highlights: 
- ObjectRawAccess renamed to ObjectAccess
- Create SubObjectAccess trait, and a set of structs which implement this, such as ScalarField<T> and NullTermByteField. These are used by code generation instead of emitting the actual ObjectAccess implementations, which means less generated code it also makes it a lot easier to define objects manually. 
-  Dropped the derive_record macro. 
- The object dictionary implementations moved to zencan-node instead of common. I don't think these are really common, and they won't be used outside of a node. 
- Use SDO buffer for atomic transfers for larger objects, up to the buffer size of 889 bytes. 
- Implement a multi-part write API on ObjectAccess, so that large objects like domains can support being written in multiple chunks when the data to be transferred is larger than the SDO buffer.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

VSCode's testing extension was unable to discover and run tests due to a **module naming conflict** between the main script `gmail_automation.py` and the package `src/gmail_automation/`. When Python attempted to import `gmail_automation.cli` from the package, it would find the root-level `gmail_automation.py` script first and treat it as the module, then fail to find the `cli` attribute within that script file.

This prevented developers from using VSCode's integrated testing features effectively.

## Solution

Renamed the main entry point from `gmail_automation.py` to `main.py` to eliminate the naming conflict while preserving all functionality. This allows Python's import system to correctly resolve `gmail_automation.cli` from the package in `src/gmail_automation/`.

## Changes Made

### Core Changes
- **Renamed**: `gmail_automation.py` → `main.py`
- **Updated**: All references across documentation, scripts, and configuration files
- **Added**: `.env` file with `PYTHONPATH=src` for proper module resolution

### Files Updated
- 📚 `README.md` - All command examples updated
- 📚 `docs/testing.md` - Tool commands updated  
- 📚 `docs/copilot-guidelines.md` - Compilation check updated
- 📚 `.github/copilot-instructions.md` - Guidelines updated
- 🔧 Development scripts (`scripts/dev.bat`, `scripts/dev.ps1`, `scripts/setup.sh`, etc.)
- ⚙️ VSCode configuration (`.vscode/tasks.json`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `.vscode/settings.json`)
- 🧪 `tests/test_integration.py` - Fixed `sys.argv` patches
- 🔄 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - Updated all tool commands

### Cleanup
- 🗑️ Removed old bytecode: `__pycache__/gmail_automation.cpython-311.pyc`
- 🗑️ Verified no temporary files remain

## Verification

author: rmaynardap
body:
## Summary

- Fix critical timing issue where global remote variables weren't inherited when creating remote data sources
- Add configurable parallelization options to prevent API rate limiting and accommodate slow connections
- Implement clean output capture for parallel terraform init operations to eliminate garbled output

## Thread Safety Analysis
1. Definitions are frozen in tfworker/commands/base.py:68 via self._app_state.freeze() which calls self.definitions.freeze()
2. But definitions have mutable runtime fields that are exempt from freezing:
 - ready: bool = False
 - needs_apply: bool = False
 - plan_file: Optional[str] = None
3. The parallel init phase is read-only: _terraform_init_single_parallel() only:
- Reads definition.plan_file (line 152)
- Calls definition.get_target_path() (line 154)
- Never modifies any definition properties
4. Definition modifications happen later in separate phases:
- plan_file is set during plan phase in tfworker/definitions/plan.py:25
- needs_apply is set during plan phase in tfworker/commands/terraform.py:200,236
- These happen after parallel init completes
5. No race conditions: Each definition is processed independently in separate threads, and they only read immutable configuration data during init.

The parallel processing is completely safe with frozen models since the init phase is purely read-only for definition properties.

## Changes

### Bug Fixes
- **Remote variable inheritance**: Fixed `_get_remotes()` to use `get_remote_vars()` instead of raw `remote_vars`, ensuring global remote variables are properly inherited when creating Terraform remote data sources
- **Output handling**: Replaced streaming output during parallel terraform init with captured output to prevent interleaved/garbled console output

  ### New Features
  - **Configurable parallelization**: Added `parallel_options` config section allowing users to control `max_preparation_workers`
  (default: 8) and `max_init_workers` (default: 4)
  - **Clean parallel logging**: Added per-definition output tagging with `[definition_name]` prefixes for easy identification

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test coverage for remote variable inheritance in data source creation
- Added tests for configurable parallelization options (defaults and custom values)
- Added tests for parallel output capture functionality
- Updated existing tests to accommodate new parallel execution paths

## Configuration Example
```yaml
  terraform:
    parallel_options:
      max_preparation_workers: 4  # Reduce for slow connections
      max_init_workers: 2         # Reduce for API rate limits
```

 ## Test Plan
- All existing tests pass (460/460)
- New tests verify global remote variable inheritance works correctly
- New tests verify configurable parallelization works
- New tests verify clean output capture during parallel operations

author: listout
body:
Problem:  Buffer menu does not handle unicode names correctly
          (after v9.1.1622)
Solution: Fix the BMHash() function (Yee Cheng Chin)

The Buffers menu uses a BMHash() function to generate a sortable number to be used for the menu index. It used a naive (and incorrect) way of encoding multiple ASCII values into a single integer, but assumes each character to be only in the ASCII 32-96 range. This means if we use non-ASCII file names (e.g. Unicode values like CJK or emojis) we get integer underflow and overflow, causing the menu index to wrap around. Vim's GUI implementations internally use a signed 32-bit integer for the `gui_mch_add_menu_item()` function and so we need to make sure the menu index is in the (0, 2^31-1) range.

To do this, if the file name starts with a non-ASCII value, we just use the first character's value and set the high bit so it sorts after the other ASCII ones. Otherwise, we just take the first 5 characters, and use 5 bit for each character to encode a 30-bit number that can be sorted.

This means Unicode file names won't be sorted beyond the first character. This is likely going to be fine as there are lots of ways to query buffers.

related: vim/vim#17403
closes: vim/vim#17928

https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/8f9de4991e84dfdc9bcc9dad0eaa2b3544ef963e

$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Simplify MCP configuration by removing `MCP_ENABLED` environment variable and fixing OAuth logic inconsistencies. MCP server is now always enabled, with OAuth protection controlled solely by `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED`.

## Changes

### Configuration Simplification
- **Remove `MCP_ENABLED`**: MCP server is now always available
- **Simplify OAuth logic**: `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED` defaults to `true`, disabled only when explicitly set to `'false'`
- **Fix redundant logic**: Eliminate duplicate OAuth decision code across multiple functions

### Code Changes
- **src/app.ts**: 
  - Simplified `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED` logic from complex OR conditions to simple false check
  - Removed redundant runtime OAuth evaluation functions
  - Use single `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED` constant throughout
- **package.json**: Remove `MCP_ENABLED=true` from npm scripts
- **tests/mcp-server.spec.ts**: Remove `MCP_ENABLED` from test environment setup
- **.env.example**: Replace `MCP_ENABLED` with `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED` documentation
- **README.md**: Update environment variable documentation

### Bug Fixes
- **Fix test failures**: `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=false npm test` now passes correctly
- **Remove 401 errors**: OAuth disabled mode works as expected
- **Consistent behavior**: No more runtime re-evaluation of OAuth settings

## Before/After

### Before (Complex Logic)
```javascript
const MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED = process.env.MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED !== 'false' && 
                          process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test' && 
                          process.env.MCP_ENABLED !== 'false';

// Multiple redundant functions with different logic
const runtimeOAuthEnabled = process.env.MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED !== 'false' && 
                           process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test' && 
                           process.env.MCP_ENABLED !== 'false';
```

### After (Simple Logic)
```javascript
const MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED = process.env.MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED !== 'false';

// Single source of truth used everywhere
return MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED ? [authMiddleware] : [];
```

## Test Results

✅ All MCP tests pass with `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=false`
✅ OAuth protection works correctly when enabled
✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Migration Guide

- Remove any `MCP_ENABLED` environment variables from your configuration
- Use `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=false` to disable OAuth protection for testing
- No other changes required - MCP is now always available

body:
I wanted to use autocmd to trigger specific actions when GhostText was
activated (namely focus my Neovide instance), and creating an autocmd using `au
nvim_ghost_user_autocommands User * ! open -a iTerm` was too broad, as it would
trigger for any User event defined by other plugins.

So I created a new autocmd that is then triggered with `nvim_exec_autocmd`, but
passing the url via the `data` callback property, only available in the
`nvim_create_autocmd` function call. It's notably more useful when writing
config files in Lua.

author: copilot
body:
Este PR resuelve todos los errores de compilación reportados en el issue, asegurando que el proyecto KybersStream_V2 compile correctamente.

## Problemas Resueltos

### 1. Dependencias Media3 Faltantes
- **Agregadas**: `media3-exoplayer-dash` y `media3-datasource-okhttp` a `libs.versions.toml`
- **Configuradas**: En `app/build.gradle.kts` para resolver imports de `DashMediaSource`, `HlsMediaSource` y `OkHttpDataSource`
- **Corrige**: Errores "Unresolved reference 'dash'" y "Unresolved reference 'okhttp'" en `OkHttpDataSourceFactory.kt` y `PlaybackManagerImpl.kt`

### 2. SettingsScreen Completamente Implementado
Creado desde cero el ecosistema completo de configuraciones:

**SettingsViewModel.kt**
- ViewModel con Hilt completo
- Gestión de estado con `SettingsUiState` 
- Integración con `UserPreferencesUseCase`
- Lógica para todas las configuraciones (tema, calidad, subtítulos, control parental, etc.)

**Componentes UI Personalizados**
- `QualitySettingItem`, `LanguageSettingItem`, `TimeFormatSettingItem`
- `SwitchSettingItem`, `ParentalControlSettingItem`, `ActionSettingItem`
- `SetPinDialog` y `AboutDialog`
- `SettingsSection` para organización

### 3. Corrección de Propiedades de Modelos
Actualizado acceso a propiedades en todas las pantallas para usar los nombres correctos del dominio:

**MoviesScreen.kt, SeriesScreen.kt, TvScreen.kt:**
```kotlin
// Antes (incorrecto)
category.name -> category.categoryName
movie.id -> movie.streamId  
series.id -> series.seriesId

// Después (correcto según modelos del dominio)
Text(category.categoryName)
key = { it.streamId }
key = { it.seriesId }
```

### 4. Smart Cast Issues
Corregido el problema de smart cast en propiedades delegadas:
```kotlin
// Antes (error de compilación)
error = uiState.error

// Después (funciona correctamente) 
error = uiState.error!!
```

### 5. Configuración de Versiones Compatible
- **AGP**: 8.0.2 (compatible con el entorno)
- **Kotlin**: 1.9.0 (en lugar de 2.2.0)
- **Compose BOM**: 2023.08.00 (estable)
- **Hilt**: 2.47 (compatible)
- **Media3**: 1.8.0 (todas las dependencias necesarias)

body:
## Overview
This enhancement introduces a sophisticated health monitoring system that establishes comprehensive verification capabilities for digital wills, significantly improving transparency and stakeholder confidence.

## Business Value
- **Enhanced Trust**: Provides verifiable proof of will validity and proper configuration
- **Proactive Management**: Enables early detection of potential issues before execution
- **Stakeholder Confidence**: Beneficiaries can confirm their awareness and verify will status
- **Audit Compliance**: Maintains detailed verification trails for legal requirements

## Technical Implementation
- **Health Scoring Algorithm**: Calculates will validity based on verification frequency and beneficiary engagement
- **Event Tracking System**: Records all verification activities with timestamp precision
- **Beneficiary Confirmation Protocol**: Allows beneficiaries to acknowledge their awareness of inheritance terms
- **Comprehensive Status Reporting**: Provides unified view of will health metrics and execution readiness

## Key Capabilities
- Real-time health score calculation based on verification patterns
- Beneficiary awareness confirmation tracking
- Detailed verification event logging
- Cross-contract integration with existing will management functions

This system operates independently of existing functionality while providing valuable oversight capabilities that enhance the overall platform's enterprise readiness and user confidence.

author: gesslar
body:
# Enhanced Variable Reference Syntax and Documentation

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for variable reference syntax in theme files, supporting three interchangeable formats:

- `$path.to.var` - Legacy/short form
- `$(path.to.var)` - Recommended parenthesized form
- `${path.to.var}` - Braced form

The evaluator has been refactored to handle all three syntaxes consistently, with improved token resolution and better handling of nested references. The README now includes a dedicated section explaining these options with examples.

Additional changes:
- Fixed code fence formatting in README examples
- Updated example themes to demonstrate variable reference styles
- Improved evaluator implementation with instance-based approach
- Added newline at end of generated theme files
- Bumped package version to 0.0.13

This change maintains backward compatibility while providing more robust options for variable references, especially in complex expressions like `fade($(std.bg.accent), 30)`.

author: copilot
body:
The keyboard toolbar's F-key canvas elements were using hardcoded dimensions that didn't adapt when fonts changed, causing visual inconsistencies with the character brush panel.

## Problem

The `#keyboard-toolbar` F-key canvases had fixed `width="8" height="16"` attributes and the `createFKeyShorcut` function only set CSS dimensions, not the actual canvas rendering dimensions. This meant:

- F-key glyphs didn't resize when switching fonts
- Visual inconsistency with the character brush panel which properly uses `font.draw()`
- Hardcoded assumptions about CP437 8x16 font dimensions

## Solution

Updated the keyboard toolbar to be truly dynamic like the character brush panel:

1. **Fixed canvas sizing** in `createFKeyShorcut()` function:
   ```javascript
   // Set actual canvas dimensions for proper rendering
   canvas.width = font.getWidth();
   canvas.height = font.getHeight();
   // Set CSS dimensions for display
   canvas.style.width = font.getWidth() + "px";
   canvas.style.height = font.getHeight() + "px";
   ```

2. **Removed hardcoded dimensions** from HTML canvas elements:
   ```html
   <!-- Before -->
   <canvas id="fkey0" class="fkey" width="8" height="16"></canvas>
   <!-- After -->
   <canvas id="fkey0" class="fkey"></canvas>
   ```

## Testing

✅ Verified F-key functionality works correctly with different font sizes  
✅ Tested dynamic resizing with fonts: 8x8, 8x16, 8x19  
✅ Confirmed visual consistency with character brush panel behavior  
✅ F-key shortcuts continue to draw characters properly on canvas  

The keyboard toolbar now properly adapts to font changes, maintaining visual consistency with the rest of the application's dynamic font system.

author: serph91p
body:
This pull request improves the handling of NFO metadata and artwork paths for media libraries, with a focus on generating correct relative paths, robust directory detection, and better fallback logic for artwork files. The changes ensure that NFO files and artwork references are more accurate and compatible with different media server setups, and that artwork is reliably available even in edge cases.

**NFO and Artwork Path Handling Improvements:**

* Added `_relative_artwork_path` and `_find_recordings_root` helper methods to robustly compute relative paths to artwork from NFO directories and to locate the recordings root containing the `.media` folder. This ensures artwork references in NFO files are accurate regardless of directory structure.
* Updated NFO generation logic to use these new helpers, ensuring that artwork paths in `tvshow.nfo`, `season.nfo`, and actor entries are always correct relative paths, improving compatibility with media scanners. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba5a795ff5985fce10c018951911a8ce5195e288b03176b7ddf02ae7631fbe2L264-R350) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba5a795ff5985fce10c018951911a8ce5195e288b03176b7ddf02ae7631fbe2L285-R364) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba5a795ff5985fce10c018951911a8ce5195e288b03176b7ddf02ae7631fbe2L307-R389)

**Directory Structure and Fallback Logic:**

* Refactored the logic for determining streamer and season directories, making it more robust and defensive to avoid misplacement of NFO files and to handle edge cases where directory names do not match expected patterns. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba5a795ff5985fce10c018951911a8ce5195e288b03176b7ddf02ae7631fbe2L233-R318) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba5a795ff5985fce10c018951911a8ce5195e288b03176b7ddf02ae7631fbe2L295-R373)
* Improved fallback mechanisms for artwork: if a thumbnail is missing, the service now attempts to copy the global poster from the artwork cache into the local folder, ensuring artwork is always present for media servers.

**Media Server Compatibility Enhancements:**

* Enhanced the creation of season poster images: season-specific posters are now created in both the season directory and as `poster.jpg`, ensuring compatibility with various media servers and their folder structure expectations.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a system to share movement patterns between promoted pieces using PromotionType mapping, addressing the need to commonize promoted piece movements as specified in the requirements.

## Problem

Previously, each piece had only one `moveRange` in its PieceData, and there was no mechanism to share common movement patterns between different promoted pieces. For example, 歩兵, 香車, 桂馬, and 銀将 all promote to pieces with identical gold-piece movement, but this commonality wasn't leveraged in the code.

## Solution

### Core Implementation

1. **Enhanced PieceDatabase**: Added `promotionPieceDataList` and `GetPromotionPieceData()` method to map PromotionType to shared movement data
2. **Smart Movement Resolution in Piece.cs**: Added `GetMoveRange()` and `GetCanStraightMove()` methods that automatically return promotion movement data when a piece is promoted
3. **Updated Movement Logic**: Modified `CheckMovablePositions()` to use the new methods instead of directly accessing piece data

### Movement Mappings

- **歩兵, 香車, 桂馬, 銀将** → `PromotionType.Gold` (金将の動き)
- **飛車** → `PromotionType.龍王` (龍王の動き) 
- **角行** → `PromotionType.龍馬` (龍馬の動き)
- **金将, 玉将** → `PromotionType.None` (成れない)

### Assets Created

- `GoldPromotion.asset` - Defines the 6-direction gold movement pattern
- `DragonHorsePromotion.asset` - Defines the 8-direction dragon horse movement  
- `DragonKingPromotion.asset` - Defines the 8-direction dragon king movement

## Benefits

- **Code Reuse**: Multiple pieces share the same promotion movement data
- **Maintainability**: Changes to promotion movement only need to be made in one place
- **Memory Efficiency**: No duplicate movement data for similar promoted pieces
- **Extensibility**: Easy to add new promotion types in the future

## Testing

Added comprehensive test script `PromotionMovementTest.cs` that verifies:
- Correct PromotionType assignments for all pieces
- Successful retrieval of promotion piece data
- Proper move range resolution for promoted pieces

The existing PieceData assets were already properly configured with the correct promotionType values, requiring no changes to the existing data.

author: haltman-at
body:
Closes #156.  (Note: the rest of this description is outdated, see comments)

The issue appears to be just the fact that touches on mobile frequently result in both `mouseup` and `touchend` events, but the button acts as a toggle, so two events has the same effect as none.

I solved it by adding a debounce timer (with a fairly arbitrary value of 10 milliseconds).  This does mean that if you click/touch rapidly, not every click/touch will register, but I couldn't find a timing that was both long enough to consistently prevent the original issue while also being short enough to consistently avoid this new one.  I think this is a rather less serious issue to introduce, so I think it's fine.

I'm not sure this is really the best solution to this problem, because you'll notice it's specific to this function.  Might be better to have some sort of more general debounce functionality related to the `mouseup`/`touchend` scenario, but I couldn't figure out how to do that.  (The other buttons are of course bouncing in this manner as well, it's just less obvious!  E.g., if next question bounces, does that really matter?)

Alternatively, for this particular case, this could perhaps better be solved by A. not having the function be a toggle, but rather set things to a specific value, and B. replacing the show/hide button with two *different* buttons, of which only one is visible at a time; then the bouncing simply wouldn't matter.  I think this way is actually probably better, except that on trying it, for some reason it didn't actually work, and also the resulting layout was wrong?

Well, I could try to debug just went wrong there, but so far I haven't bothered, because meanwhile right here's a crude simple solution that already works.

body:
## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeout controls, leading to excessive CPU consumption.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Implemented 2-second timeout check to prevent long-running operations
- Reduced path finding max_depth from 10 to 5 for better performance

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core functionality remains intact
- Tested with production workload patterns

## Impact
This change will significantly reduce CPU usage and prevent pod restarts while maintaining the essential functionality of the graph processing algorithm.

author: copilot
body:
This PR completely transforms the existing SBR-RS sequence-based recommender system into a comprehensive SaaS platform with modern architecture, Vietnamese language support, and LLM integration capabilities.

## 🎯 Problem Analysis

The original SBR-RS was a powerful Rust library for sequence-based recommendations but had several limitations for modern deployment:

- **Outdated Dependencies**: Using yanked crates from 2018-2019 that prevented compilation
- **No API Layer**: Library-only with no web service capabilities  
- **Limited Language Support**: No Vietnamese language processing
- **Single-Tenant**: No multi-tenancy support for SaaS deployment
- **No LLM Integration**: Missing modern AI capabilities for content understanding

## 🚀 Complete SaaS Transformation

### Modern Architecture
- **REST API**: Built with Axum web framework for high-performance async handling
- **Multi-Tenancy**: Complete tenant isolation using PostgreSQL Row Level Security
- **Authentication**: JWT + API key authentication with role-based access control
- **Database Layer**: Modern SQLx with migrations and repository patterns
- **Microservices Ready**: Containerized with Docker and Kubernetes configurations

### Vietnamese LLM Integration
- **PhoBERT Embeddings**: Vietnamese BERT model integration for semantic understanding
- **Text Processing**: Vietnamese tokenization, sentiment analysis, and keyword extraction
- **Auto-Categorization**: Intelligent product categorization for Vietnamese e-commerce
- **Content Features**: Hybrid collaborative + content-based recommendations

### Industry-Specific Support
The platform now supports multiple industries with specialized features:

```rust
// E-commerce Vietnamese product categorization
let category = processor.classify_vietnamese_category(
    "Áo sơ mi nam công sở", 
    Some("Áo sơ mi cao cấp cho doanh nhân")
);
// Returns: "thời trang"

// Sentiment analysis for feedback
let sentiment = processor.analyze_vietnamese_sentiment(
    "Sản phẩm rất tốt, chất lượng tuyệt vời!"
);
// Returns: 0.8 (positive sentiment)
```

## 📊 Business Model & Scalability

### SaaS Pricing Tiers
- **Startup ($99/month)**: 10K API calls, basic analytics
- **Growth ($299/month)**: 50K API calls, advanced features  
- **Enterprise ($999/month)**: 500K+ calls, white-label options

### API-First Design
```bash
# Simple recommendation request
curl -X POST https://api.sbr-rs.com/api/v1/recommendations/recommend \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user123", "num_recommendations": 10}'

# Vietnamese context support  
curl -X POST https://api.sbr-rs.com/api/v1/recommendations/recommend \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_vietnam", "context": {"category": "thời trang"}}'
```

## 🏗️ Technical Implementation

### Database Schema
Complete multi-tenant schema with:
- Tenant isolation and management
- Model versioning and deployment tracking  
- Interaction history and feedback collection
- API usage analytics and billing data

### LLM Processing Pipeline
```rust
// Vietnamese text processing pipeline
pub async fn extract_content_features(
    &self,
    title: Option<&str>,
    description: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<ContentFeatures, LLMError> {
    let processed_text = self.preprocess_vietnamese_text(text)?;
    let embeddings = self.phobert.encode_texts(&[processed_text]).await?;
    let sentiment = self.analyze_vietnamese_sentiment(text)?;
    let category = self.classify_vietnamese_category(title, description)?;
    
    Ok(ContentFeatures {
        embedding: embeddings[0].clone(),
        sentiment_score: Some(sentiment),
        category: Some(category),
        // ... additional features
    })
}
```

### Production-Ready Deployment
- **Docker**: Multi-stage builds for optimized containers
- **Kubernetes**: Auto-scaling deployment configurations
- **Monitoring**: Distributed tracing and metrics collection
- **Security**: JWT authentication, API rate limiting, data encryption

## 📚 Comprehensive Vietnamese Documentation

All documentation has been created in Vietnamese to support the local market:

- **Architecture Guide** (`docs/vi/KIẾN-TRÚC-HỆ-THỐNG.md`): Complete system architecture explanation
- **Development Plan** (`plan/KẾ-HOẠCH-PHÁT-TRIỂN.md`): 20-week development roadmap  
- **API Documentation** (`docs/vi/API-DOCUMENTATION.md`): Comprehensive API reference
- **Project Structure** (`docs/vi/CẤU-TRÚC-DỰ-ÁN.md`): Code organization guide

## 🔄 Migration Path

The changes maintain backward compatibility while adding new capabilities:

1. **Original Models**: LSTM and EWMA models preserved with enhanced APIs
2. **New Hybrid Model**: Combines collaborative filtering with LLM content features
3. **Gradual Migration**: Existing users can migrate incrementally to SaaS features

## 🎯 Market Impact

This transformation targets the Vietnamese and Southeast Asian markets with:

- **Local Language Support**: First-class Vietnamese text processing
- **Industry Templates**: Pre-configured solutions for e-commerce, media, education, finance
- **Quick Integration**: RESTful APIs for easy integration with existing systems
- **Scalable Infrastructure**: Handle growth from startup to enterprise scale

The platform is now ready for production deployment and can serve as a competitive SaaS offering in the Vietnamese market with unique advantages in language processing and industry-specific optimizations.

This PR implements comprehensive mobile controls for the Ocean Adventure 3D game and fixes critical CI/CD pipeline issues to ensure reliable builds and deployments.

## Mobile Controls Features

### Virtual Joystick Control
- **Draggable joystick** positioned in the bottom-left corner for horizontal and forward/backward movement
- **Physics-based knob movement** with realistic constraints and smooth visual feedback
- **Optimized touch handling** with proper event prevention and touch-action CSS properties

### Swimming Controls
- **Touch buttons** (↑/↓) in the bottom-right corner for swimming up and down
- **Continuous movement** while buttons are pressed, integrated into the game loop
- **Visual feedback** with active states and smooth transitions

### Enhanced Touch Interactions
- **Canvas swipe gestures** for additional movement control with configurable sensitivity
- **Multi-touch support** allowing simultaneous joystick and button interactions
- **Touch event management** with proper start/move/end/cancel handling

## CI/CD Pipeline Improvements

### Fixed Script Reliability
- Updated npm scripts to use `npx` instead of fragile `node_modules` paths
- Fixed `lint`, `format:check`, `type-check`, and `analyze:bundle` scripts for consistent CI execution
- Resolved module resolution issues that caused build failures

### GitHub MCP Integration
- Added Model Context Protocol configuration (`.mcp.json`) for enhanced AI-assisted development
- Created comprehensive GitHub Copilot instructions with project context and coding guidelines
- Configured development tools and preferences for better code assistance

## Responsive Design

The mobile controls automatically appear on devices with screen width ≤768px using CSS media queries:

```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
    #mobileControls {
        display: block;
    }
}
```

Desktop keyboard controls (WASD/Arrow keys) remain fully functional and unaffected.

## Technical Implementation

- **Minimal code changes**: Enhanced existing `setupTouchControls()` placeholder method
- **Clean architecture**: Separated virtual joystick, mobile buttons, and canvas touch handling
- **Performance optimized**: Mobile-specific settings with reduced complexity for smooth 30-60 FPS
- **Comprehensive testing**: Added unit tests covering mobile device detection, DOM elements, and touch event handling
- **Reliable CI/CD**: Fixed all script execution issues for consistent builds and deployments

The implementation follows the technical architecture outlined in `COPILOT_PLAN.md` Phase 4 requirements, providing touch-based swimming controls, virtual joystick navigation, responsive UI, and now includes robust CI/CD pipeline fixes.

Fixes #6.

This PR implements a new public API endpoint that allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific event without authentication.

## Changes Made

### New API Endpoint
- Added `GET /events/{event_id}` public endpoint that returns event details with associated organization information
- No authentication required, making it accessible to any user

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds support for parsing BigInt literals in all numeric bases, fixing an issue where only decimal BigInt literals were supported.

## Problem

The parser previously supported decimal BigInt literals like `123n` but failed to parse hexadecimal, binary, and octal BigInt literals:

```javascript
var x = 123n;                    // ✅ Works
var x = 0x9e3779b185ebca87n;     // ❌ "Unexpected token ILLEGAL"
var x = 0b1010n;                 // ❌ "Unexpected token ILLEGAL"  
var x = 0o777n;                  // ❌ "Unexpected token ILLEGAL"
```

## Solution

The issue was that the `scanHexLiteral`, `scanBinaryLiteral`, and `scanOctalLiteral` methods in the scanner only returned `NumericLiteral` tokens and didn't check for the BigInt suffix `n`.

This PR adds BigInt suffix detection to all three methods:

- **`scanHexLiteral`**: Now detects `n` suffix and returns `BigIntLiteral` tokens for hex BigInts
- **`scanBinaryLiteral`**: Now detects `n` suffix and returns `BigIntLiteral` tokens for binary BigInts  
- **`scanOctalLiteral`**: Now detects `n` suffix and returns `BigIntLiteral` tokens for octal BigInts

## Testing

Added comprehensive test coverage in `test_bigint_literals()` that verifies:
- All numeric bases work correctly (decimal, hex, binary, octal)
- Proper token types are generated (`BigIntLiteral` vs `NumericLiteral`)
- Correct values are parsed and preserved
- Raw string representations are maintained
- Invalid BigInt formats (decimals with `n`) correctly fail

## Results

All BigInt literal formats now work correctly:

```javascript
var x = 123n;                    // ✅ Works (existing)
var x = 0x9e3779b185ebca87n;     // ✅ Now works
var x = 0b1010n;                 // ✅ Now works  
var x = 0o777n;                  // ✅ Now works
var x = 0X123n;                  // ✅ Now works (uppercase)
var x = 0B1010n;                 // ✅ Now works (uppercase)
var x = 0O777n;                  // ✅ Now works (uppercase)
```

All existing tests continue to pass with no regressions.

Fixes #5.

The problem with `TROOT::GetLibDir()` was that it either hardcodes the install directory inside it if `ROOTLIBDIR` was set (which is the case for `gnuinstall=ON`), or it assumes that it's always called `lib` and is inside the `$ROOTSYS`, which might or might not be set. This is broken if the `CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR` is different from the default `lib`.

This commit suggests to automatically figure out the ROOT library directory instead.

This pull request introduces several new features and improvements, primarily focused on animation support, data processing enhancements, and dependency updates. Notably, it adds support for handling large video files, introduces a new CLI tool for generating protein-ligand binding animations, and provides additional data summaries for processed datasets. There are also updates to the Python dependencies to support new features and improve performance.

**Animation and Media Support:**
- Added Git LFS tracking for `.mp4` files in `.gitattributes`, and included three new animation video files (`bg-1.mp4`, `bg-2.mp4`, `bg-3.mp4`) in the `Animations` directory to support media assets in the project. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-618cd5b83d62060ba3d027e314a21ceaf75d36067ff820db126642944145393eR1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c77a0bc50cbc430f72d810159e643d81059734adb15ab0ab3d2749d79d2333a2R1-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ec04f4b4696d841fee83a97dffd4e144421e640b5cccd554c0b42ed048333442R1-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0b9ef431db4c1bdb2adbaa766786ee0f1b805d8d7841f6039e8c18938295eb6eR1-R3)

author: vlordier
body:
## 🏗️ Major Repository Restructuring

This PR completely reorganizes the CharMorph codebase from a flat structure into a properly organized Python package with clear separation of concerns.

## 📁 New Structure

### Before (Flat Root)
- 15+ Python files cluttering the root directory
- Mixed responsibilities at the same level
- Hard to navigate and understand relationships
- Third-party code mixed with core functionality

### After (Organized Packages)
```
charmorph/
├── core/          # Core morphing, rigging, asset management
├── ui/            # Blender user interface components  
├── editors/       # Character editing tools
├── utils/         # Utility functions and helpers
└── third_party/   # External dependencies (updater, YAML)
```

## ✨ Key Improvements

### 🧹 **Clean Organization**
- **Separated by function**: Core logic, UI, editing tools, utilities
- **Isolated dependencies**: Third-party code properly contained
- **Clear module boundaries**: Easy to understand what each package does
- **Documentation ready**: README, TODO, licenses at root level

### 🔧 **Technical Enhancements** 
- **All imports updated**: Full compatibility maintained
- **Proper packaging**: Complete `__init__.py` files with documentation
- **Quality assurance**: Pre-commit hooks passing, code compiles successfully
- **Future-ready**: Foundation for testing infrastructure

### 📝 **Maintainability**
- **Better discoverability**: Find functionality quickly
- **Reduced complexity**: Clear separation of responsibilities  
- **Easier onboarding**: New developers can understand structure immediately
- **Scalable foundation**: Room for growth and new features

## 🛠️ Migration Details

### File Movements
- **Core functionality** → `charmorph/core/`
- **UI components** → `charmorph/ui/`  
- **Editing tools** → `charmorph/editors/`
- **Utilities** → `charmorph/utils/`
- **Auto-updater** → `charmorph/third_party/updater/`
- **YAML library** → `charmorph/third_party/yaml/`

### Import Updates
- Updated 100+ import statements across all modules
- Maintained backward compatibility
- Fixed cross-module dependencies
- Preserved original functionality

## ✅ Quality Assurance

- **Code compilation**: All modules compile successfully
- **Import resolution**: No broken imports or missing modules
- **Pre-commit hooks**: Passing with proper third-party ignores
- **Code formatting**: Consistent style maintained
- **Linting**: Clean with appropriate exceptions for third-party code

## 🔮 Future Benefits

This restructuring provides a solid foundation for:
- **Testing framework**: Clear structure for unit/integration tests
- **Documentation**: Organized module documentation
- **Plugin architecture**: Easier to extend with new functionality  
- **Code navigation**: IDE tools work better with proper package structure
- **Collaboration**: Multiple developers can work on different areas without conflicts

## 🧪 Test Plan

- [x] All Python files compile without errors
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass successfully  
- [x] Code quality maintained (ruff, formatting)
- [x] Import statements resolve correctly
- [x] Package structure follows Python best practices
- [x] Documentation and licenses properly positioned

author: ehsan-saradar
body:
## Description

After extensive testing, this PR switches Solana swap parsing to use **transaction simulation**. By simulating transactions we can extract token inputs/outputs and SOL deltas directly, instead of hard-coding logic for each swap program.
Previously, parsing swaps required adding and maintaining support for each individual swap provider program. This was error-prone and not scalable as new providers or versions appear. Simulation provides a provider-agnostic way to detect actual token flows, making the solution more robust and future-proof.

author: pauloandrehxh
body:
## O que este PR faz?
Este PR introduz a estrutura de navegação principal para a aplicação SIG-Recipes. As principais mudanças são:

* Criação do loop principal do programa em `main.c` com uma estrutura `do-while` e `switch-case`.
* Implementação de um menu com 4 opções: Tela Principal, Sobre, Créditos e Sair.
* Adição das funções `telaSobre()` e `telaCreditos()` com as informações do projeto e dos desenvolvedores.
* Inclusão de funções utilitárias `limparTela()` e `pressioneEnterParaContinuar()` para melhorar a experiência do usuário.

## Como testar?
Para garantir que as mudanças estão funcionando corretamente, siga estes passos:

1.  Faça o checkout desta branch (`feat/menu-navegacao`).
2.  Compile e execute o programa (`gcc main.c -o sig_recipes` e depois `./sig_recipes`).
3.  Verifique se tá tudo ok.

## Observações 
* A `telaPrincipal()` por enquanto só exibe uma mensagem de placeholder. As funcionalidades de receitas (adicionar, listar, etc.) serão implementadas em branches futuras.
* O código para `limparTela()` foi feito de forma a ser compatível com Windows (`cls`) e Linux/macOS (`clear`). A parte dessa função que utiliza `#ifdef _WIN32`, `#else` e `#endif` não é C, é uma **diretiva de pré-processador**, que analisa o código antes do compilador.

body:
## Summary

This PR improves the user experience by moving the display name editing functionality from the Profile tab to the Account Settings, positioning it logically above the skin type section for better information architecture.

## 🎯 **User Experience Improvement**

### **Before**: Display name editing in Profile tab
- "Edit Display Name" action in Profile view alongside other account actions
- Separated from other account configuration options
- Profile view cluttered with editing functionality

### **After**: Display name editing in Account Settings
- Display name section positioned above skin type in Account Settings
- Consolidated with other account-related configurations
- Cleaner Profile view focused on account overview
- Logical grouping of related settings

## ✨ **Key Changes**

### **AccountSettingsView.swift** (+74 lines)
- **New Display Name Section**: Added above skin type section with clean design
- **Inline Edit Button**: Compact "Edit" button with icon for easy access
- **Environment Integration**: Uses `@EnvironmentObject` for `AuthenticationManager`
- **System Prompt Handling**: Automatically shows name edit for new users when settings open
- **Consistent Styling**: Matches existing account settings design patterns

### **MainContentView.swift** (-32 lines)
- **Removed ProfileActionRow**: Eliminated "Edit Display Name" from profile actions
- **Cleaned State Variables**: Removed `showingNamePrompt` and `newDisplayName` state
- **Simplified Profile View**: Focus on account overview rather than editing
- **Environment Passing**: Added `environmentObject(authManager)` to AccountSettingsView

## 🏗️ **Technical Implementation**

### **Display Name Section Design**
```swift
// Clean section with inline edit button
VStack(spacing: 16) {
    HStack {
        Image(systemName: "person.circle")
        Text("Display Name")
        Spacer()
        Button("Edit") { /* edit action */ }
    }
    HStack {
        Text(authManager.userDisplayName)
        Spacer()
    }
}
```

### **Maintained Functionality**
- ✅ **Name Validation**: Same validation rules and error handling
- ✅ **System Prompting**: Automatic prompting for new users without names
- ✅ **Component Reuse**: Uses existing `NameInputView` component
- ✅ **AuthManager Integration**: Proper display name updates and persistence

### **Better Information Architecture**
```
Account Settings:
├── Safety Warning (if applicable)
├── 📝 Display Name (NEW - moved from Profile)
├── 👤 Skin Type
├── 👶 Age Range  
├── 💊 Medical Information
└── 🌡️ Temperature Unit
```

## 📱 **User Flow**

1. **Accessing Name Edit**: Profile → Account Settings → Display Name → Edit
2. **New Users**: Automatic prompt when opening Account Settings (if name missing)
3. **Existing Users**: Manual edit via inline "Edit" button
4. **Validation**: Same robust validation as before

## 🧪 **Testing**

- [x] Build succeeds without errors
- [x] Display name section renders correctly above skin type
- [x] Edit button opens name input sheet
- [x] Name updates properly save and reflect in UI
- [x] Profile view is cleaner without edit action
- [x] Environment object properly passed to AccountSettingsView
- [x] System prompting still works for new users
- [x] Existing NameInputView component works as expected

## 📊 **Benefits**

### **User Experience**
- **Better Organization**: All account settings in one logical location
- **Reduced Cognitive Load**: Cleaner Profile view focused on overview
- **Intuitive Navigation**: Name editing where users expect account settings

### **Code Quality**
- **Separation of Concerns**: Profile for viewing, Settings for editing
- **Reduced Complexity**: Simplified Profile view with fewer state variables
- **Consistent Patterns**: Follows existing Account Settings design language

### **Maintainability**
- **Centralized Settings**: All account configuration in AccountSettingsView
- **Component Reuse**: Leverages existing NameInputView component
- **Clear Responsibilities**: Each view has a focused purpose

## 🔄 **Breaking Changes**

None - this is a pure UX improvement that maintains all existing functionality while improving information architecture.

## Title

Fix Vertex AI tool call deepcopy issue with Pydantic models

## Relevant issues

Fixes #12096

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)

- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem

## Type

Bug Fix

## Changes

- Added `safe_copy_optional_params()` helper function that falls back to shallow copy when deepcopy fails
- Replaced `deepcopy(optional_params)` calls in Vertex AI completion handlers (lines 2698 and 2742) with the safe copy function
- This fixes the issue where Pydantic models with list return types in tool definitions cause serialization errors with deepcopy
- Added comprehensive tests in `tests/test_litellm/test_vertex_tool_call_deepcopy.py` that verify:
  - Pydantic models with list return types are handled correctly
  - Regular dict objects still use deepcopy when possible
  - Edge cases like empty dicts work properly

## Test Results

All 3 new tests pass:
```
============================= test session starts ==============================
platform darwin -- Python 3.11.13, pytest-7.4.4, pluggy-1.6.0 -- /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11
```

author: copilot
body:
Fixes the contact text styling that was intended to be applied in PR #3 but didn't land due to an empty commit.

## Problem
The previous PR #3 merged with 0 changed files, so the intended styling changes for email, phone, and location contact text were never applied. The contact information was displaying in the default text color (#e0e0e0) with dotted underlines, instead of the site's primary cyan color.

## Solution
Updated the `.contact-text` CSS rules in `style.css` to:
- Change color from `var(--text-color)` to `var(--primary-color)` (cyan #00f0ff)
- Remove dotted underline by setting `border-bottom: none`
- Simplify hover state by removing the `border-bottom-color` property

## Changes Made
```css
/* Before */
.contact-text { color: var(--text-color); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px dotted rgba(255,255,255,0.25); }
.contact-text:hover { text-decoration: none; border-bottom-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.5); }

/* After */
.contact-text { color: var(--primary-color); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: none; }
.contact-text:hover { text-decoration: none; }
```

This affects the email, phone, and location links in the hero section while keeping the LinkedIn styling unchanged (as it uses the `.link-only` class).

![Contact Section After Fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2cc43ceb-09c3-42da-8645-56b719163a97)

The contact information now displays consistently with the site's cyan theme and has a cleaner appearance without the distracting dotted underlines.

author: somratdutta
body:
# Add REST Catalog Support for Iceberg Writes

Enables direct writes to Iceberg tables via REST catalog, removing PyIceberg dependency.

## Changes
- REST catalog integration for Iceberg write operations
- `DataLakeCatalog` database engine with REST backend
- `IcebergS3` table engine REST catalog support

## Settings
- `allow_experimental_database_iceberg`: Enable DataLakeCatalog engine
- `allow_experimental_insert_into_iceberg`: Enable Iceberg INSERT operations
- `storage_catalog_type='rest'`: Use REST catalog
- `storage_catalog_url`: REST catalog endpoint

## Usage
```sql
SET allow_experimental_database_iceberg=true;
CREATE DATABASE demo ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('http://localhost:8182/v1', 'user', 'pass') 
SETTINGS catalog_type='rest', warehouse='demo';

CREATE TABLE demo.table (x String) ENGINE = IcebergS3('s3://bucket/path/', 'user', 'pass') 
SETTINGS storage_catalog_type='rest', storage_catalog_url='http://localhost:8182/v1';

SET allow_experimental_insert_into_iceberg=1;
INSERT INTO demo.table VALUES ('data');
```

Tested with Tabulario REST catalog and MinIO storage.
